reference.title: Forward Lunge (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step forward and lower, exhale as you push back to standing.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.7 s push back

prescription.tempo: Controlled step, 1-2 s down, push back in about 1 s

cues.text: Stand tall, feet hip width, hands on hips.
Take a long step forward and land heel first.
Breathe in and lower the back knee toward the floor; back heel up.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to step back to standing.
Stand tall and reset; alternate legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep the front knee over the 2nd-3rd toe; shorten the range if needed.
Lengthen the step and keep the weight in the front heel.
Lower under control and stop just above the floor.

mistakes.mistake: Short step (front knee far past the toes)
mistakes.fix: Step long enough that the front shin is near vertical at the bottom.

kinematics.peak: 80 cm forward (72.2 cm between ankle centres once the back heel is up)
kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); a step about one leg length was suggested as optimal for strength training (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈102°, 14 cm above the floor (knee joint centre)
kinematics.norm: Lowers to just above the floor, about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Upright to slightly forward; more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)

kinematics.peak: Step 0.8 s, 1.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.75 s up, step back 0.85 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: Hip, knee and ankle joint moments in the single-legged squat, forward lunge and reverse lunge (J Athl Train; PMC4641539)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Park et al. 2016, comparative analysis of lunge techniques: forward, reverse, walking lunge (ISBS proceedings)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: shorten the range and keep the front knee over the middle of the foot.
Balance concerns: hold a wall or chair with one hand.
Knee pain: start with the rear lunge, which loads the knee less (PMC4641539).

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539), and more so with the trunk inclined forward (Farrokhi 2008).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539), and more so with the trunk inclined forward (Farrokhi 2008).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk tall and the pelvis level.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
